items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: Max Hart, who was the theatrical agent... The man who had his numbers copyrighted was our manager, Max Hart.

ctx.x: Could you I hate to interrupt you again But as you go along Could you give me the details on the records you made I'd like to hear about the What you did for Columbia and how that happened Well on the Columbia

Max Hart fixed a date for us to go up there and make a record Now this place was located at 16 Broadway It was only a block away from Rides and Rambus We went up there one morning to record And they told us to play over the piece And when they did that They were all putting their hands to their ears Some was in the back hitting on hammers Making noises They didn't care to put us in the right position And they'd taken two lousy records And they paid us $250 for nothing For Indiana and Docktown Stutters Ball We…

to make it equal to the other. There was no reason of volume here. You hear the cut or be cut down with the Dixieland Jazz Band. And I believe that's what gave us the edge on all of it because there was no time that I'd ever have to take down on any record record when it went 12 hours. I could still hold that heart in my mouth and play it. Now this might be bragging, but I did it many times. Till the dancers toppled over, I'd stayed in playing.
